items.title: Pakistan's leadership stresses need for unity, reforms as nation celebrates Independence Day
items.description: Pakistan’s civilian and military leadership has stressed the need for unity and reforms as the nation celebrates 79 years of independence today. According to state-run Radio Pakistan , the day dawned with a 31-gun salute in Islamabad and a 21-gun salute at the provincial headquarters. A change of guards ceremony was also held at the mausoleum of Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah in Karachi. Flag hoisting ceremonies were also held at the Supreme Court and the Federal Constitutional Court in Islamabad. ‘Pakistan’s security linked to peace in our neighbourhood’ In his message, President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to Quaid-i-Azam, those behind the Pakistan Movement and those who sacrificed their homes, security and livelihoods in the struggle for a homeland. “But independence is not only a historic achievement. It is also a responsibility that each generation must carry forward. The Pakistan that was created through the democratic will of its people must continue to grow stronger, more secure and more prosperous. Our task is not only to remember what earlier generations achieved, but to add to it through our own work,” he said. The president said that the past year had reminded citizens of the strength of the Pakistani nation. Recalling last year’s brief military conflict with India, he said, “The events surrounding Marka-i-Haq demonstrated that Pakistan seeks peace, but also possesses the resolve and capacity to defend its sovereignty and national interests. The lesson of strength is ultimately a lesson of responsibility. A country that can defend itself must also use its strength to prevent conflict, protect peace and serve the interests of its people.” He said that the security and stability enjoyed today had come at a great cost, paying tribute to the martyrs of the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and police. “Their courage and commitment have helped safeguard our nation against external aggression and the threat of terrorism. The people of Pakistan remain deeply grateful for their service,” he said. He also highlighted Pakistan’s efforts to facilitate dialogue in the region. “Pakistan has effectively used its channels of communication, its geographical location and diplomatic capital to encourage dialogue and de-escalation at a time when wider conflict could have serious consequences for the region and the world,” he said. He reiterated that all disputes must be ultimately addressed through dialogue and diplomacy. “Our security is linked to the peace and stability of our neighbourhood and the world at large. Pakistan will continue to support efforts that reduce tensions, protect regional stability and create conditions for cooperation,” he said. The president also went on to say that the country must focus on the work that will determine Pakistan’s future. “We must strengthen our economy, create greater opportunities for our young people, improve education and skills, strengthen institutions through a series of governance, economic and social reforms to ensure that the benefits of development and democracy reach every part and community of the country,” he said. “Pakistan’s greatest strength is its young people. Across the country and around the world, they are demonstrating their talent in science, technology, business, education and the creative industries. Our responsibility is to give them the education, skills and opportunities they need to realise their potential. By investing in our youth today, we are investing in Pakistan’s future,” he added. “For ordinary Pakistanis, national progress is measured in practical terms. It means a young person finding the skills and opportunity to build a career. It means a family being able to access quality education and healthcare. It means farmers, workers, traders and businesses being able to plan for the future with greater confidence. The strength of Pakistan will ultimately be judged by whether our national progress improves the lives of its people,” President Zardari said. He also voiced Pakistan’s support for the people of occupied Kashmir, saying Pakistan will continue to support a peaceful resolution of the dispute in accordance with the aspirations of its people and the relevant United Nations resolutions. On Afghanistan, the president said that Pakistan had always respected and supported the national sovereignty of our neighbour Afghanistan and expected the same reciprocity. “It is sad that the current interim regime of Afghanistan is allowing and supporting a cocktail of terror groups to use their soil for launching attacks against neighbouring countries including Pakistan. It is sad the Taliban regime of Afghanistan is collaborating with India in launching terror attacks against Pakistani civilians and security personnel. They are doing this to distract us from the peace building efforts of Pakistan, recognised by the entire world,” he said. “I warn them to stop these evil actions against the people of Pakistan and assure all and sundry that the armed forces of Pakistan are capable of defeating these evil designs,” he said. He ended his message by calling on the nation to contribute to the country’s progress in whatever field they serve. ‘Pakistan committed to defending its national interests’ Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also began his message by paying tribute to the founding leaders of Pakistan, saying the nation owed the fulfilment of its dream of an independent homeland to their vision, statesmanship and sacrifices. Highlighting the government’s economic achievements over the past two-and-a-half years, PM Shehbaz said the country had successfully navigated challenging circumstances to achieve economic stability and was now moving towards becoming a developed economy. He noted that remittances from overseas Pakistanis had increased by $11.3 billion over the past two years, which he termed a reflection of their confidence in government policies. The prime minister said harnessing modern information technology, promoting innovation-driven industrial and agricultural development, creating employment opportunities and establishing a world-class education and skills system remained among the government’s top priorities. Paying tribute to the armed forces, the prime minister said the military, under the leadership of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, had demonstrated exemplary unity and courage during Marka-i-Haq, adding another chapter to the country’s history of defence. He said Pakistan remained committed to defending its national interests, including its right to water resources, and reiterated that the country would continue to play its role as a responsible nation and a stabilising force for regional and global peace. He cited the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye as testimony to the country’s growing strategic role in the region. The prime minister also expressed solidarity with the people of occupied Kashmir and the Palestinian people. He said lasting peace in South Asia was contingent upon a diplomatic resolution of the Kashmir dispute in line with United Nations resolutions, international law and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people. The prime minister also paid tribute to the martyrs of the armed forces and law enforcement agencies who sacrificed their lives for the country, and called upon all segments of society, particularly political parties, to work together for national unity, integrity and the advancement of national interests. He concluded his message by praying for Pakistan’s continued progress and dignity in the comity of nations. ‘Pakistan’s strength lies in the unity of its people’ CDF Munir, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf and Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu also issued a message to mark Independence Day. According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the armed forces paid tribute to the Quaid and those whose sacrifices resulted in a sovereign Pakistan. “Their vision, courage and resolve remain a guiding force for the nation and continue to inspire us to uphold the principles and ideals of Pakistan,” the statement said. “The armed forces of Pakistan respectfully acknowledge the supreme sacrifices of our martyrs, the services of our veterans, the dedication of law enforcement personnel and the contributions of every Pakistani who has served the nation. Their courage and selfless service have bolstered Pakistan’s resilience and safeguarded its independence, security and national interests,” it added. “As guardians of Pakistan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the armed forces reaffirm their unwavering resolve to defend the motherland against all threats, uphold the Constitution and discharge the sacred trust reposed in them by the people of Pakistan. United with the nation, the armed forces will remain steadfast in preserving peace and stability while creating an environment conducive to national progress and prosperity,” the statement said. “Pakistan’s strength lies in the unity and collective resolve of its people. On this Independence Day, let us renew our commitment to the enduring principles of faith, unity and discipline, strengthen national cohesion, promote tolerance and work together towards a secure, stable and prosperous Pakistan,” it concluded. Dar reaffirms determination to safeguard country’s sovereignty In his message on the occasion, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar recalled Marka-i-Haq and reaffirmed Pakistan’s determination to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity. “We commemorated the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq, recalling Pakistan’s resolute and successful response to Indian aggression in 2025,” he said in a televised address to the nation. “The occasion reaffirmed our determination to safeguard Pakistan’s sovereignty, security and territorial integrity while remaining firmly committed to international law, responsible state craft and the pursuit of regional peace.” At the outset of his address, the deputy PM extended greetings to Pakistanis and expatriates on the Independence Day, saying we commemorate the day “to pay tribute to Quaid-i-Azam whose visionary leadership, unwavering resolve and steadfast commitment transformed the aspirations for a separate homeland into reality”. He also paid honour to the leaders and workers of the Pakistan movement whose “courage, dedication and countless sacrifices laid the foundations of our independent state”. Dar said that since independence, the country had made “remarkable strides across diverse fields guided by the enduring principles of unity, faith and discipline”. “Today we are a resilient nation of more than 250 million people bound together by our shared history, collective heritage and common aspirations,” he added. He also noted that the country’s achievements in education, science and technology, economic development, sports, culture and other fields “reflect the talent, determination and immense potential of our people”. The deputy PM also mentioned Pakistan’s “strengthened” position on the international stage over the past eight decades. “Our expanding diplomatic engagement, growing economic connectivity and partnerships, and deepening defence and security cooperation reflect Pakistan’s confidence and its commitment to contributing to a peaceful, stable and prosperous region and world.” He also mentioned the defence accord signed by Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia last week, saying the “historic agreement reflects our shared resolve to deepen strategic cooperation, strengthen collective security and address evolving regional and international peace and security challenges”. He also paid special tribute to armed forces, police and paramilitary forces of the country, saying their “courage, professionalism and unwavering commitment remain a bulwark of our national security”. Dar noted the country always “stood for peace, dialogue, cooperation and mutual respect among nations”. He referred to last year’s conflict with India and said the events “underscored the urgent need of peaceful resolution of longstanding disputes, particularly the Jammu and Kashmir dispute which remains a source of instability in our region”. “Pakistan will continue to extend its principles, moral, political and diplomatic support to the Kashmiri people in their just struggle for the realisation of their right to self-determination in accordance with the relevant UNSC resolutions,” he added. On the occasion, he urged people to “draw renewed inspirations from the ideals and vision that led to the creation of Pakistan”. “Let us reaffirm our collective resolve to strengthen our institutions, uphold our national unity, harness the potential of our people and build a stronger more prosperous and peaceful Pakistan for generations to come,” he concluded. Kashmir stands ‘shoulder to shoulder’ with Pakistan: AJK president Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) President Chaudhry Latif Akbar, addressing a flag-hoisting ceremony in Muzafarabad, expressed gratitude to Pakistan for standing by the Kashmiri people and advocating their cause at international forums, as well as repeatedly calling for implementation of the relevant United Nations resolutions. He highlighted the “centuries-old” bonds between Kashmir and Pakistan, saying the relationship was rooted in shared history, culture, religion, traditions and aspirations and had found political expression in the Kashmiri leadership’s July 19, 1947, resolution seeking accession of the princely state to Pakistan. “Pakistan has also stood with the people of Kashmir through difficult periods and fought wars in defence of its position on the Kashmir dispute,” he said, adding that Kashmiris would never forget Pakistan’s steadfast support. Akbar reiterated that the people of AJK stood “shoulder to shoulder” with the people of Pakistan and said their destinies were intertwined. Additional input from Tariq Naqash

items.title: Centre médical de Kindi : double passation de charges à la tête du Centre médical et du COGES
items.description: BURKINA-BOULKIEMDE-KINDI-CENTRE-MEDICAL-PASSATION-DE-CHARGES Centre médical de Kindi : double passation de charges à la tête du Centre médical et du COGES Kindi, 14 août 2026 (AIB) – Le centre médical de Kindi a abrité, le mercredi 12 août 2026, une cérémonie de double passation de charges. Placée sous la présidence du secrétaire général de la mairie de Kindi, Yacouba Soré, représentant le président de la délégation spéciale, cette transition administrative a concerné à la fois la direction du centre médical et le bureau du Comité de gestion (COGES). La cérémonie s'est déroulée dans la salle de réunion de l'infrastructure sanitaire, en présence d'une équipe cadre du district sanitaire de Nanoro conduite par Gérard Konaté, ainsi que de nombreux agents de santé et les membres du COGES. Après deux ans et demi de fonction, le Dr Isaac Bayili a cédé son fauteuil de médecin responsable à son successeur, le Dr Kadré Derra. Parallèlement, le bureau sortant du COGES, dirigé par Jean-Pierre Zoundi après plus de quatorze années de gestion, a passé le témoin à la nouvelle équipe élue, pilotée par Christian Sompougdou. Prenant la parole au nom des autorités, le représentant du président de la délégation spéciale et l'équipe cadre du district ont tour à tour salué le travail abattu par les partants. Le Dr Isaac Bayili a été félicité pour son sens de l'écoute, son dévouement et ses sacrifices malgré la modicité des moyens disponibles. Des vœux de plein succès lui ont été formulés pour la suite de sa carrière. Quant au président sortant du COGES, Jean-Pierre Zoundi, les autorités ont magnifié ses quatorze années d'engagement bénévole et de don de soi au service des populations de Kindi. Aux nouveaux responsables, notamment le Dr Kadré Derra et le président entrant Christian Sompougdou, les autorités ont souhaité la bienvenue et un plein succès dans l'accomplissement de leurs nouvelles charges, tout en rappelant le caractère hautement bénévole et citoyen de la mission confiée au COGES. À leur tour, les sortants ont exprimé leur gratitude aux autorités administratives, sanitaires et coutumières ainsi qu'à l'ensemble des agents pour l'accompagnement dont ils ont bénéficié durant leur magistère, tout en demandant l'indulgence pour les éventuels manquements. En réponse, les entrants ont pris l'engagement de mériter la confiance placée en eux. Le Dr Kadré Derra a promis de tout mettre en œuvre pour consolider les acquis et maintenir le cap de la bonne gouvernance sanitaire. De même, s'exprimant au nom du nouveau bureau du COGES, le commissaire aux comptes Lucien Kaboré a réitéré la disponibilité et la détermination de son équipe à œuvrer aux côtés de l'administration pour le rayonnement du centre médical. La cérémonie s'est achevée par la signature officielle des documents administratifs et leur remise aux différentes parties prenantes, dans une ambiance empreinte de cordialité. Agence d'information du Burkina CS/PB/AS/ATA

items.title: Nadra launches locally made QR code-based identity cards
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) on Wednesday launched a new chipless National Identity Card (NIC) built around a secure QR code, replacing the imported microchip used for the past 14 years. The card has been manufactured domestically by the National Security Printing Company (NSPC) in Karachi in line with Nadra’s technical and security specifications, a statement issued by the authority on Friday said. Instead of a chip, the card will carry a secure QR code that can be scanned and verified on a smartphone through Nadra’s Pak Identity (PakID) mobile application, it added. The federal government approved the issuance of the new card on February 23 this year. The code will contain the cardholder’s information and photograph. According to Nadra, this will allow institutions to enter individuals’ names, addresses and other identity details more easily and consistently in their systems while reducing data entry errors. The card will also display a family number and symbols to denote persons with disabilities, senior citizens, organ donors and citizens of Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The cardholder’s name and address will be printed in both Urdu and English, Nadra added. The visible and covert security features of the card have been “updated to meet current requirements and align with domestic manufacturing capabilities”, the statement said. Nadra said the chip-based Smart NIC introduced about 14 years ago could not be fully utilised as chip readers and supporting infrastructure were never widely available. The QR-based card addresses this gap, being verifiable through an ordinary smartphone or software connected to a camera, it said. Telecom operators, banks, hospitals, the Pakistan Railways, police and other authorised institutions will also be provided with software to read and verify the QR code, Nadra said. The rollout will be phased, with the QR code-based card replacing the standard CNIC from Friday, it said, adding that from January 2027, it will be issued for all categories, including NICs for Overseas Pakistanis (Nicops) and Juvenile Cards. In the final phase, the Pakistan Origin Card (POC) will also transition to the chipless format, according to the statement. Nadra clarified that all previously issued identity cards would remain valid until their expiry dates. In February, the government notified amendments to the National Identity Card Rules, 2002 and the Pakistan Origin Card Rules, 2002 to modernise the country’s identity document framework. Part of these reforms included the statutory introduction of the QR code — a scannable barcode containing horizontal and vertical lines, dots, and patterns — as a defined security and verification feature. The amendments further authorised the use of a QR code or “any other technological feature”, in lieu of the current microchip, enabling Nadra to adopt evolving verification technologies without repeated rule amendments.

Les États-Unis veulent évaluer la loyauté de leurs alliés de l’OTAN
items.description: Washington a recemment envoye aux pays membres de l'OTAN un questionnaire visant a mesurer leur soutien a la politique de Donald Trump, sur fond de possible reduction de la presence militaire americaine en Europe. Selon un article de Bloomberg, qui a revele l'existence du document le 14 août, les allies doivent notamment preciser s'ils ont apporte un « soutien public » a la politique etrangere des etats-Unis et quelles restrictions ils ont imposees a l'utilisation de bases militaires par les forces americaines. Le document va au-dela des seules questions de securite. Washington veut egalement savoir si ses partenaires achetent des armes aupres d'entreprises americaines et s'ils soutiennent des regles susceptibles de limiter l'acces de ces societes aux contrats de defense europeens. Les pays sont aussi interroges sur leur position concernant le principe du « Made in Europe » dans le secteur de l'armement. Cette demarche intervient alors que l'administration Trump mene un reexamen de six mois de son dispositif militaire en Europe, dont les conclusions sont attendues en decembre. Dans le meme temps, Washington cherche a transferer une part croissante des responsabilites militaires et financieres aux membres europeens de l'Alliance. Des divergences de plus en plus visibles au sein de l'OTAN Les questions posees par Washington renvoient directement a plusieurs differends recents avec certains de ses allies. Celles concernant l'acces aux bases militaires portent notamment sur les operations americaines au Moyen-Orient et dans l'hemisphere occidental. L'Espagne avait ainsi refuse de soutenir les frappes americaines contre l'Iran et interdit l'utilisation de ses bases a cette fin. Le questionnaire fait egalement reference, de maniere indirecte, a l'Iran ainsi qu'a l'operation americaine visant Nicolás Maduro au Venezuela. Ces episodes illustrent les divergences qui peuvent apparaître lorsque certains membres de l'Alliance refusent de suivre automatiquement les initiatives de Washington. La demarche a d'ailleurs ete mal accueillie par plusieurs pays de l'OTAN. D'apres les sources citees par Bloomberg, certains allies y voient une tentative de les pousser vers un alignement politique et ideologique en echange du maintien des garanties de securite americaines. L'agence estime qu'une telle evolution pourrait modifier sensiblement l'equilibre des relations transatlantiques herite de l'apres-guerre. Washington reduit progressivement son role militaire en Europe Le questionnaire s'inscrit dans une revision plus large de la presence americaine sur le continent. Le 28 juillet, le responsable du Pentagone Elbridge Colby avait confirme le lancement de cet examen, en soulignant que l'administration Trump entendait transferer davantage de responsabilites militaires aux allies europeens. La reduction des effectifs americains avait deja ete evoquee au printemps. Donald Trump avait alors annonce de nouvelles diminutions de la presence militaire des etats-Unis en Europe, au-dela du retrait deja prevu de 5 000 militaires d'Allemagne. La legislation americaine interdit toutefois une baisse des effectifs sous le seuil de 76 000 militaires en Europe sans justification supplementaire. L'ampleur et la repartition d'un eventuel retrait restent donc a determiner. Le secretaire general de l'OTAN, Mark Rutte, a qualifie le reexamen americain de decision « logique et positive », compte tenu de la hausse des depenses militaires europeennes et canadiennes. Un representant de l'Alliance a egalement confirme a Bloomberg que des discussions etaient en cours avec Washington, sans commenter directement le questionnaire. Les decisions attendues d'ici la fin de l'annee devraient ainsi preciser jusqu'ou les etats-Unis comptent reduire leur presence militaire directe en Europe. Elles permettront egalement de voir dans quelle mesure Washington entend desormais conditionner davantage son engagement aupres de ses allies a leur alignement politique, a leurs choix militaires et a leurs achats dans le secteur de la defense.

items.title: 2 suspects in fatal attacks on Lahore cops killed in Muridke fire exchange, say police
items.description: LAHORE: Two men who allegedly shot dead three police officials in Lahore on Thursday were killed during an exchange of fire with law enforcers at a house in Muridke where they had held a family hostage, police sources told Dawn . Police officials identified the suspects as a father-son duo, Fayyaz Butt and Rehan Butt, saying that they were killed in a joint operation by Lahore police, Counter-Terrrorism Department (CTD) personnel, Sheikhpura police and Elite Force personnel on Friday morning after an hours-long chase from Lahore to Muridke. The suspects held the driver of a Lahore Waste Management Company vehicle at gunpoint and forced him to keep on driving to reach Muridke, the officials said. According to police, they allegedly shot dead two policemen in Lahore’s Badami Bagh area and one at Yateem Khana Chowk, Multan Road, besides injuring three on Thursday night. Initial police inquiries showed that the first armed attack was carried out by Rehan and his accomplices in Badami Bagh. The martyred officials were identified as Sub-Inspector (SI) Adeel Ashiq and Constable Asad. An hour later, the suspects allegedly targeted policemen deployed at the headquarters of the banned Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP) on Multan Road and opened indiscriminate firing. On Friday, a senior official who coordinated the joint operation against the suspects told Dawn a third suspect, identified as Tariq, managed to flee. His last location was reported as Bagh in Azad Jammu Kashmir (AJK). AJK police and the law enforcement agencies from Punjab were working to trace and arrest him, he said. Regarding Friday’s operation, the official said Fayyaz and Rehan were traced to a seminary in Muridke. Law enforcers surrounded it after reaching the site while the seminary’s management claimed that the two were not present there. To verify the claim, police seized the seminary’s DVR, but found that the cameras were not working, he said, adding that the DVR was sent to Lahore for forensic analysis. Meanwhile, law enforcers received information that the suspects had gone toward River Ravi and were hiding in a forest, the official said. On the directions of IG police Punjab Abdul Kareem, the police used thermal drones to trace the suspects in the forest, he said, adding that the suspects moved to a densely populated area as they realised they were being traced. “They barged into a house, took the family hostage and threatened to kill them,” he said, adding that the suspects opened fire on the police personnel when they reached there. During the exchange of fire, Rehan and Fayyaz were killed, he said. He said Tariq had separated from them and fled to AJK during the chase. After Thursday’s attack, a police official had told Dawn that the incidents seemed to be an act of revenge. Rehan’s brother, Faizan Butt, was allegedly killed in an encounter with a CTD team, which reportedly included SI Adeel, a few years back, the official said. Faizan was reportedly working for the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and he was involved in the killing of some police officials, the police official said. He added that SI Adeel had told police higher-ups in 2024 that he was receiving life threats from Rehan. Following his complaint, a first information report was registered against Rehan in November 2024 with Shafiqabad police. According to the FIR, Adeel had alleged that he had received a WhatsApp call from Rehan, who had threatened to kill him.

items.title: Rethink MMDCE elections – Dr Tando proposes MP-led appointment model
items.description: Governance and public policy analyst Dr Solahudeen Tando has proposed a fundamental rethink of Ghana’s continuing debate over the election of Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs). He argued that the country should consider transferring appointment responsibility from the President to Members of Parliament rather than creating another layer of public elections. Under the proposed model, MPs would appoint MMDCEs as development representatives within a regulated professional framework, with clear qualification and competence standards and safeguards against unrestricted political patronage. Dr Tando argues that the proposal deserves consideration because Ghana’s political culture has already transformed MPs into de facto development agents, although their formal constitutional role remains principally legislative and representative. He made the proposal at the National Dialogue on Decentralisation and Responsive Governance in Accra, where he presented a discussion paper titled, “ The Next Frontier of Democratic Decentralisation: Strengthening District Assemblies as Territorial Platforms of the Ghanaian State for Integrated Public Service Delivery and Local Development .” The dialogue brought together government officials, local government practitioners, academics, civil society organisations, development partners and other sector stakeholders to examine the future of Ghana’s decentralisation system. Dr Tando questioned whether the proposed election of MMDCEs adequately resolves the deeper institutional problems confronting local governance. “What real problem does another election of MMDCEs seek to solve?” he asked. He argued that the question becomes particularly important when the existing political and institutional realities surrounding MPs are examined. According to him, MPs routinely campaign on roads, schools, health facilities, sanitation, jobs and other local development priorities. Constituents consequently hold them politically accountable for development outcomes, although formal responsibility for local development rests principally within the District Assembly system. He noted that the Government’s 2026 Position Paper on constitutional reform has itself acknowledged this institutional evolution, describing MPs as having become development agents in their constituencies “by default” and rejecting a recommendation that DACF allocations to MPs be prohibited. Dr Tando said the development raises a wider accountability question that Ghana must confront before creating another independently elected political office within substantially the same territorial development space. “If both the MP and MMDCE acquire separate democratic legitimacy within substantially the same development space, who ultimately bears political accountability for constituency development when things go right or wrong?” he asked. He said the proposed alternative would shift appointment control away from the Presidency and place responsibility closer to an already elected constituency representative. Under his proposal, however, an MP would not possess unrestricted discretion to appoint any preferred political actor. Dr Tando proposes a regulated system under which relevant public institutions provide professional safeguards around the appointment process. The Public Services Commission could establish appropriate professional and person specifications, while the role and performance expectations of the MMDCE would align with the applicable district development framework and national development planning architecture. He argues that such safeguards could make competence an integral part of the appointment process while retaining identifiable political accountability. The proposal, he acknowledged, represents a significant departure from both the current presidential appointment system and competing proposals for direct popular election. However, he argued that Ghana’s local government debate should not treat an additional election as synonymous with decentralisation. According to him, election addresses the method through which an officeholder acquires political legitimacy, whereas effective decentralisation also requires attention to authority, administrative capacity, resources, planning, coordination and accountability. Dr Tando further questioned whether Ghana should create two separately elected political centres that face substantially overlapping constituency-development expectations without first defining the relationship between their mandates. He maintained that his proposal seeks to institutionalise an existing political reality rather than create an entirely new role for MPs. “We continue to hold MPs politically accountable for local development irrespective of the formal institutional location of development responsibility. Legislation alone is unlikely to erase that deeply embedded political expectation,” he argued. He said the central reform question is therefore whether Ghana should continue to treat that political evolution as an anomaly or deliberately structure, regulate and make it accountable. Dr Tando also called for a broader reconceptualisation of District Assemblies beyond their conventional treatment as local administrative structures. He proposed that the District Assembly should be understood as “a territorial platform through which the fragmented functional state becomes an integrated local service experience in the delivery of public value.” Under that conception, decentralisation should ultimately be assessed through the experience of citizens at the local level rather than principally through the number of functions formally transferred or institutions established. “Decentralisation must make the state coherent at the point where the citizen experiences it,” he said. Dr Tando acknowledged that the MP-led appointment proposal requires further constitutional and institutional scrutiny, including safeguards against excessive concentration of political authority and arrangements for districts that contain more than one parliamentary constituency. He nevertheless argued that unconventional proposals should remain open to scrutiny as Ghana searches for durable consensus on local government reform. “Perhaps MP appointment is not ultimately the answer. I am open to that. But we should not discard the institutional problem simply because one proposed answer is unconventional,” he said.

items.title: La Tunisie et la Libye lancent un vaste appel d’offres conjoint pour l’exploration pétrolière et gazière en Méditerranée
items.description: La Tunisie et la Libye relancent leur appel d'offres petrolier et gazier dans le bassin offshore de Gabes-Tripoli, avec une ouverture prevue le 7 septembre 2026. Pilotee par la societe commune Joint Oil, la procedure porte sur deux volets : l'exploration d'un bloc de 3 000 km² et le developpement du gisement transfrontalier de Zarat. Creee en 1988, Joint Oil gere les ressources de cette zone maritime commune aux deux pays. L'appel d'offres restera ouvert jusqu'au 31 decembre 2026. Les compagnies disposant d'une experience confirmee dans l'exploration et le developpement offshore pourront acceder a une salle de donnees virtuelle geree par le cabinet Moyes & Co. Les candidats retenus seront informes le 26 fevrier 2027, avant les attributions officielles prevues d'ici au 30 avril 2027. Joint Oil presentera egalement les projets a Londres, le 9 septembre 2026 lors du Mediterranean, Middle East & Africa Scout Group, puis les 29 et 30 septembre au World Energy Summit. Un bassin offshore a fort potentiel Le volet exploration concerne une zone situee dans des eaux de 80 a 120 metres de profondeur. Le bloc est deja couvert par environ 1 900 km² de donnees sismiques 3D, auxquels s'ajoutent 6 500 km de profils sismiques 2D. Il dispose egalement des resultats de cinq puits d'exploration fores entre 1976 et 2010. Cinq principales cibles ont ete identifiees : Faisal, Hadaf, Siraj Est, Siraj Ouest et Zarat profond. Leurs ressources moyennes en place depasseraient 1,6 milliard de barils de petrole et 87,8 milliards de m³ de gaz naturel. Hadaf concentre le potentiel petrolier le plus important, avec un peu plus d'un milliard de barils estimes en place. Siraj Ouest apparaît comme la principale cible gaziere, avec environ 48,1 milliards de m³ de gaz, auxquels s'ajouteraient 358 millions de barils de petrole. Le bloc se trouve par ailleurs a proximite de plusieurs champs deja exploites, notamment Bouri, Al Jurf et Bahr Essalam cote libyen, ainsi qu'Ashtart, Miskar et Didon cote tunisien. Cette proximite avec des installations existantes pourrait faciliter le developpement d'eventuelles decouvertes et leur integration aux infrastructures energetiques regionales. Zarat, un projet commun au cœur du developpement a ce programme d'exploration s'ajoute un projet plus avance : le developpement de Zarat. Decouvert par Marathon Oil en 1992, le gisement est situe a cheval sur la frontiere maritime tuniso-libyenne. Zarat contiendrait 266 millions de barils de petrole et de condensats ainsi que 31,1 milliards de m³ de gaz en place. Les reserves recuperables sont estimees a 72 millions de barils et 23,6 milliards de m³ de gaz. Sa mise en valeur necessitera plusieurs accords entre la Tunisie et la Libye, notamment sur le partage de la production, l'unification des ressources et l'exploitation commune du gisement. Parmi les solutions envisagees figurent le raccordement de plusieurs puits a une unite de production offshore et l'utilisation des infrastructures regionales pour l'evacuation du petrole. Avec cette relance, Tunis et Tripoli cherchent ainsi a mieux valoriser leurs ressources offshore communes et a approfondir une cooperation energetique bilaterale engagee depuis plusieurs decennies. Le projet s'inscrit ainsi dans une logique de developpement conjoint d'un bassin partage, reposant directement sur les interets et les capacites des deux pays voisins.

items.title: Meet Nigeria’s Daniel Umemezie, named US national youth poet laureate
items.description: Daniel Umemezie has been named the 2026–2027 US National Youth Poet Laureate, becoming the 10th young poet to hold the prestigious title and the second Nigerian-American to receive the honour. Umemezie follows in the footsteps of Salome Agbaroji, who became the first Nigerian-American to be named US National Youth Poet Laureate in 2023. A gifted Nigerian-American poet, Umemezie uses his writing to explore heritage, identity and the complexities of the Nigerian-American experience. His poetry reflects the richness of his experiences while connecting questions of culture and identity with the realities of growing up between different worlds. Through his work, Umemezie has emerged as a distinctive young literary voice, using poetry not only as a form of creative expression but also as a way to tell stories and explore experiences that resonate with wider audiences. His appointment marks another notable achievement for Nigerian-American representation in the US literary space, following Agbaroji’s historic appointment three years ago. Umemezie’s achievement has also been celebrated as an example of how young people can use creativity and storytelling to lead, inspire and make an impact. The National Youth Poet Laureate title recognises outstanding young poets in the United States and provides a platform for young literary voices to reach wider audiences. Umemezie’s selection places him among a growing generation of young poets using their voices to explore culture, identity and contemporary life. His achievement also highlights the continued contributions of Nigerian-American young people to the arts and creative industries in the United States. The post Meet Nigeria’s Daniel Umemezie, named US national youth poet laureate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Saisies de navires russes : Londres s'inquiète du manque de moyens pour faire face à Moscou
items.description: Le Royaume-Uni ne disposerait pas d'une puissance de feu suffisante pour empecher la Russie de s'emparer de navires britanniques dans l'hypothese d'une confrontation de ce type, rapporte le 13 août le Telegraph , citant plusieurs sources du secteur de la defense. Selon les interlocuteurs du quotidien, les inquietudes portent principalement sur l'Indo-Pacifique, ou la presence militaire britannique est jugee trop limitee pour faire face a une eventuelle saisie de bâtiments par la Russie. Cette situation est notamment attribuee a la reduction progressive des moyens de la Royal Navy . L'ancien chef de la marine britannique, l'amiral Alan West, a vivement critique cette evolution, estimant que les gouvernements successifs avaient laisse la flotte diminuer au point qu'elle ne dispose desormais plus d'un nombre suffisant de navires pour remplir sa mission de protection de la navigation mondiale. Dans l'ocean Indien, la marine britannique ne dispose actuellement que de deux patrouilleurs susceptibles d'assurer la protection de navires du Royaume-Uni : le HMS Tamar et le HMS Spey, tous deux faiblement armes. Pour Alan West, ces bâtiments servent avant tout a assurer une presence britannique dans la region. Il a rappele qu'il y a encore une trentaine d'annees, quatre ou cinq navires y etaient deployes, contre seulement deux aujourd'hui. Face a cette faiblesse des moyens disponibles, l'ancien ministre britannique de la Defense, Ben Wallace, a suggere de s'appuyer davantage sur les allies. Il a notamment evoque la possibilite de solliciter la France afin de mieux repartir les missions a l'echelle mondiale, notamment pour assurer des fonctions d'escorte ou de protection. Le 12 août, le president russe Vladimir Poutine a prevenu que Moscou repondrait de maniere symetrique si des pays occidentaux procedaient a la saisie de navires russes. « Ils ont pense qu'il etait possible de saisir nos navires et de vendre les biens voles. Il s'agit, bien sûr, de piraterie et de vol. Et si cela se concretise, nous serons contraints de repondre de facon symetrique. Et pas necessairement dans les eaux ou ils prevoient d'attaquer nos navires. Mais la ou nous le jugerons approprie. N'importe ou. Y compris dans la zone de responsabilite de la flotte du Pacifique », a-t-il fait savoir. Le vice-president du Conseil de securite russe, Dmitri Medvedev , a ensuite developpe cette position. Invoquant le principe de reciprocite, il a affirme que la Russie pourrait prendre pour cible tout navire marchand se trouvant dans ses eaux ou dans des eaux neutres si elle avait suffisamment de raisons de soupconner que celui-ci transporte une cargaison destinee aux interets de l'adversaire.

items.title: Après des mois de controverse, la réforme de la profession d’adoul entre en vigueur
items.description: Le Maroc s’apprête à tourner une page importante dans l’organisation de la profession d’adoul. Publiée au Bulletin officiel n° 7533 en vertu du dahir n° 1.26.58 du 28 juillet 2026, la loi n° 51.26 relative à l’organisation de la profession entrera en vigueur dans un délai de 90 jours. Son adoption met un terme à un long parcours législatif marqué par d’intenses débats politiques et professionnels, des mouvements de protestation ainsi qu’une intervention décisive de la Cour constitutionnelle, qui avait censuré plusieurs dispositions du texte avant sa révision par le Parlement. Au-delà des ajustements exigés par le juge constitutionnel, cette réforme redessine en profondeur les conditions d’accès à la profession, les modalités de son exercice, les mécanismes de contrôle et de discipline ainsi que l’organisation de ses instances représentatives. Elle introduit également de nouvelles exigences en matière de numérisation et d’archivage des actes. Un accès à la profession davantage encadré Le nouveau texte consacre l’adoul comme un auxiliaire de justice exerçant une profession libérale. À ce titre, il est tenu de respecter les principes d’intégrité, de probité, d’impartialité et de discrétion professionnelle qui fondent la crédibilité de l’authentification adoulaire. Les conditions d’accès à la profession sont désormais clairement définies. Les candidats devront être de nationalité marocaine, de confession musulmane, âgés d’au moins 21 ans et de moins de 45 ans à la date du concours. Une dérogation est toutefois prévue pour certains fonctionnaires titulaires d’un doctorat et justifiant de dix années d’ancienneté effective dans la fonction publique. Le législateur a également élargi la liste des diplômes ouvrant droit à la candidature. Les titulaires de licences en charia, en fondements de la religion, en études islamiques ou en sciences juridiques, dans les filières de droit public ou privé, pourront se présenter au concours, sous réserve de remplir les autres conditions relatives à la moralité, à la jouissance des droits civils, à la situation vis-à-vis du service militaire et à l’aptitude physique. La loi écarte en revanche les personnes ayant fait l’objet de condamnations définitives pour certaines infractions, notamment les crimes financiers ou les faits de falsification, ainsi que celles sanctionnées disciplinairement pour des actes portant atteinte à l’honneur de leur profession. L’accès à la profession reste subordonné à la réussite à un concours, à l’accomplissement d’un stage de deux ans et à la validation d’un examen de fin de formation. Cette période comprend six mois de formation théorique et dix-huit mois de pratique au sein d’une étude adoulaire. Certaines catégories professionnelles pourront néanmoins bénéficier d’exemptions, selon des conditions précises fixées par la loi. Une profession soumise à de nouvelles obligations La réforme impose aux adouls un cadre d’exercice plus rigoureux. Chaque professionnel devra disposer d’une étude dans le ressort du tribunal de première instance où il est affecté, être inscrit auprès du conseil régional compétent, prêter serment et souscrire une assurance couvrant sa responsabilité civile professionnelle. Le texte précise également les incompatibilités professionnelles. L’exercice de la fonction d’adoul ne pourra être cumulé avec plusieurs métiers juridiques ou judiciaires, notamment ceux de magistrat, avocat, notaire, huissier de justice, traducteur assermenté ou expert judiciaire. Certaines activités commerciales ou fonctions dirigeantes au sein des sociétés demeurent également incompatibles avec la profession. En parallèle, les obligations déontologiques sont renforcées. Les adouls devront conserver le secret professionnel, tenir des registres spécifiques relatifs aux actes et aux opérations financières et respecter les tarifs réglementaires. Toute perception de rémunérations non prévues par les textes est expressément interdite. La loi interdit également toute situation de conflit d’intérêts. Les adouls ne pourront ni tirer un avantage personnel des actes qu’ils rédigent ni accomplir des opérations susceptibles de remettre en cause leur indépendance ou leur neutralité. Leur responsabilité professionnelle est par ailleurs clairement engagée. Ils répondront non seulement de leurs propres erreurs, mais également de celles commises par leurs collaborateurs ou leurs stagiaires lorsqu’elles causent un préjudice aux usagers. Autre nouveauté : les professionnels âgés de plus de 70 ans devront produire chaque année un certificat médical attestant de leur aptitude à poursuivre leur activité. Ils seront également soumis à une obligation de formation continue tout au long de leur carrière. Numérisation et archivage : la réforme entre dans l’ère digitale L’un des volets majeurs de la réforme concerne la modernisation des procédures. La loi confirme la compétence des adouls pour recevoir et établir les actes auxquels la législation confère un caractère authentique ou que les parties souhaitent formaliser sous cette forme. Elle leur impose toutefois des obligations accrues de vérification concernant l’identité, la qualité juridique et la capacité des parties, ainsi que la conformité des documents présentés. Les règles de rédaction des actes sont également précisées, qu’il s’agisse de leur forme, de leur contenu, de leur numérotation ou des modalités de signature. Le recours à la signature électronique qualifiée est désormais admis conformément à la législation en vigueur. La conservation des actes fait aussi l’objet d’un traitement particulier. Les originaux, copies officielles et registres devront être conservés de manière permanente, tandis que les pièces justificatives annexes seront archivées pendant une durée de dix ans. Surtout, la réforme instaure un système d’archivage électronique généralisé. Les actes établis par les adouls devront être déposés quotidiennement sur une plateforme numérique placée sous la supervision du ministère de la Justice. Cette mesure s’inscrit dans le mouvement plus large de digitalisation des services juridiques et judiciaires engagé ces dernières années. Le texte réglemente également le témoignage collectif, ou « lafif », en fixant à douze le nombre minimal de témoins et en précisant les modalités de leur audition et de la validation de leurs déclarations. Cette question figurait parmi les points ayant suscité l’attention de la Cour constitutionnelle lors de l’examen de la précédente version du texte. Contrôles renforcés et sanctions graduées La nouvelle architecture légale repose sur un système de contrôle à plusieurs niveaux. Les études adoulaires feront l’objet d’une inspection annuelle au minimum par le juge chargé de la documentation. Les conseils régionaux disposeront également de prérogatives de contrôle, tandis que des inspections pourront être menées par le procureur général du Roi compétent ou par l’autorité gouvernementale chargée de la justice. La loi prévoit la possibilité de suspendre temporairement un adoul pour une période maximale de trois mois lorsqu’il fait l’objet de poursuites disciplinaires ou pénales liées à des faits portant atteinte à l’honneur de la profession. L’échelle des sanctions disciplinaires est elle aussi précisée. Elle va du simple avertissement jusqu’à la révocation définitive, en passant par le blâme et la suspension temporaire de l’exercice. Les garanties procédurales sont maintenues : l’adoul concerné pourra consulter son dossier, assurer sa défense et se faire assister par un avocat ou un confrère. Les décisions disciplinaires demeureront susceptibles de recours devant la justice administrative. Dans le même temps, la profession bénéficie d’une protection juridique renforcée. Les adouls continueront à bénéficier des protections prévues par le Code pénal dans l’exercice de leurs fonctions. Ils disposeront d’un sceau, d’une carte professionnelle et d’une tenue réglementaire dont les caractéristiques seront fixées par voie réglementaire. La loi interdit par ailleurs toute forme de démarchage ou de publicité destinée à attirer la clientèle. Elle autorise néanmoins, sous certaines conditions, la création de sites internet professionnels. Les contrevenants s’exposent à des amendes comprises entre 15.000 et 30.000 dirhams. Une nouvelle gouvernance pour la profession La réforme réorganise également les institutions représentatives des adouls. L’Instance nationale des adouls est confirmée comme une personne morale dotée de l’autonomie financière. Chargée de coordonner l’action des conseils régionaux et de défendre les intérêts de la profession, elle devient l’unique interlocuteur habilité à représenter les adouls auprès des administrations et des tiers. Le texte définit les attributions de ses différents organes, notamment l’assemblée générale, le président et le bureau exécutif. Le président sera élu pour un mandat de quatre ans non renouvelable et devra justifier d’au moins quinze années d’exercice effectif de la profession. Les conseils régionaux, quant à eux, regrouperont les adouls exerçant dans le ressort des cours d’appel. Chaque conseil devra compter au minimum quarante professionnels. La loi introduit également des dispositions visant à garantir une représentation proportionnelle des femmes adouls au sein des organes dirigeants. Enfin, les dispositions transitoires prévoient l’abrogation des textes incompatibles, notamment la loi n° 16.03 relative au plan de justice. Elles ouvrent aussi aux copistes actuellement en exercice la possibilité d’intégrer la profession d’adoul, sous réserve de déposer leur demande dans les délais prévus et de suivre une formation spécifique de trois mois. Par cette réforme, le législateur entend à la fois consolider les garanties juridiques offertes aux citoyens, moderniser l’authentification adoulaire et adapter l’organisation de la profession aux exigences contemporaines de gouvernance et de numérisation. The post Après des mois de controverse, la réforme de la profession d’adoul entre en vigueur appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Boké : le Consortium SMB-Winning lance une formation de deux mois pour 73 jeunes
items.description: Face aux exigences technologiques et opérationnelles des métiers d’aujourd’hui, la qualification professionnelle constitue un véritable levier pour renforcer l’employabilité des jeunes. C’est dans ce cadre que la direction générale du Consortium SMB-Winning a lancé, ce vendredi 14 août 2026, à l’École régionale des arts et métiers (ERAM) de Boké, un programme de formation professionnelle destiné à 73 jeunes issus des communautés impactées des préfectures de Boké et de Télimélé. D’une durée de deux mois, cette formation vise principalement à doter les bénéficiaires de compétences adaptées aux besoins réels du marché de l’emploi et aux exigences des secteurs minier, industriel et artisanal. Pour le premier vice-maire de la commune urbaine de Boké, Abdoulaye Manè, cette initiative illustre l’engagement des entreprises minières, notamment la SMB, en faveur de leur responsabilité sociétale. Il a salué les efforts consentis pour renforcer les compétences des jeunes et mieux les préparer à leur avenir professionnel. Au nom du Collège des techniciens et professionnels des métiers (CPTM), Boubacar Kanté a rappelé que cette cérémonie marque le début d’un parcours de formation de deux mois pour les jeunes de Boké et de Télimélé. Il a particulièrement insisté sur l’importance de la qualification professionnelle des jeunes dans les différents domaines de compétence. Il a également salué l’engagement du Consortium SMB-Winning dans la valorisation de la jeunesse et l’adaptation de ses compétences aux exigences du marché de l’emploi, une démarche qui, selon lui, s’inscrit dans la vision du président Mamadi Doumbouya à travers le programme Simandou 2040. De son côté, le directeur général du département des relations communautaires du Consortium SMB-Winning et coordinateur du projet Simandou, Wu Kiong, a déclaré que cette session de formation constitue une nouvelle étape importante dans la concrétisation des engagements de la SMB en matière de responsabilité sociétale, de promotion du contenu local et d’accompagnement durable des communautés riveraines de ses zones d’opération. Il a souligné que le développement durable d’une région repose notamment sur la valorisation de son capital humain, la formation professionnelle de sa jeunesse et la création d’opportunités concrètes d’insertion socioprofessionnelle. Selon lui, la présence du Consortium SMB-Winning s’inscrit également dans une vision à long terme visant à bâtir un partenariat solide, responsable et mutuellement bénéfique avec les communautés. « Chers jeunes de Boké et Télimélé, l’opportunité qui vous est offerte aujourd’hui est le fruit d’un partenariat ambitieux. Mais sa réussite dépendra de votre engagement et de votre détermination », a-t-il lancé aux bénéficiaires. En ouvrant officiellement les travaux de cette session de formation destinée aux 73 jeunes de Boké et de Télimélé, le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Boké, Sékouba Traoré, a estimé que cette initiative témoigne de la volonté du Consortium SMB-Winning de « construire la Guinée avec les Guinéens ». Il a également cité plusieurs réalisations et initiatives communautaires du Consortium SMB-Winning, notamment la construction d’une ligne ferroviaire de 135 kilomètres, le lancement des travaux de construction de la route reliant Boké à Télimélé ainsi que la formation professionnelle de 73 jeunes des deux préfectures. Pour le représentant de l’administration préfectorale, la formation de la jeunesse constitue un investissement essentiel pour l’avenir. « Former la jeunesse, c’est tourner les pages d’un passé sombre marqué par les manifestations de rue, les perturbations des activités minières et les grèves illimitées », a-t-il déclaré. Cette nouvelle initiative du Consortium SMB-Winning entend ainsi contribuer au renforcement des compétences locales et favoriser une meilleure insertion des jeunes des communautés riveraines dans le tissu économique et professionnel de la région.

items.title: Osun Election: NUJ calls for safety of journalists covering polls
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Osun State Council, has urged political parties, security agencies, election officials and other stakeholders to protect journalists covering Saturday’s governorship election. In a statement signed by its Chairman, Adeyemi Aboderin, and Secretary, Olalekan Akindoju, the council said journalists must be allowed to carry out their duties without intimidation, harassment, assault, arrest or obstruction. The NUJ also advised journalists to prioritise their safety, avoid confrontations and promptly report any incident that threatens their safety or ability to work. The union encouraged journalists to use the WaFlo WhatsApp-enabled live election incident reporting system deployed by the International Press Centre. The AI-assisted platform allows journalists to report and document incidents involving threats, harassment, attacks, detention, equipment seizure, denial of access and other forms of interference. Journalists can access the Safe Media WhatsApp prompt through the designated channel or send “safemedia” to https://dub.sh/safemedia, or by typing “safemedia” and sending the text to 0805 877 8053. The council called on security agencies to recognise journalists as important participants in the democratic process and provide adequate protection at polling units, collation centres and other election locations. It also urged journalists to maintain professionalism, impartiality and accuracy while covering the election. The NUJ stressed that all stakeholders must work together to preserve peace and ensure voters can exercise their rights freely while journalists report the electoral process safely. items.title: Rethink MMDCE elections – Dr Tando proposes MP-led appointment model
items.description: Governance and public policy analyst, Dr Solahudeen Tando has proposed a fundamental rethink of Ghana’s continuing debate over the election of Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs), arguing that the country should consider transferring appointment responsibility from the President to Members of Parliament rather than creating another layer of public elections. Under the proposed model, MPs would appoint MMDCEs as development representatives within a regulated professional framework, with clear qualification and competence standards and safeguards against unrestricted political patronage. Dr Tando argues that the proposal deserves consideration because Ghana’s political culture has already transformed MPs into de facto development agents, although their formal constitutional role remains principally legislative and representative. He made the proposal at the National Dialogue on Decentralisation and Responsive Governance in Accra, where he presented a discussion paper titled, “The Next Frontier of Democratic Decentralisation: Strengthening District Assemblies as Territorial Platforms of the Ghanaian State for Integrated Public Service Delivery and Local Development.” The dialogue brought together government officials, local government practitioners, academics, civil society organisations, development partners and other sector stakeholders to examine the future of Ghana’s decentralisation system. Dr Tando questioned whether the proposed election of MMDCEs adequately resolves the deeper institutional problems confronting local governance. “What real problem does another election of MMDCEs seek to solve?” he asked. He argued that the question becomes particularly important when the existing political and institutional realities surrounding MPs are examined. According to him, MPs routinely campaign on roads, schools, health facilities, sanitation, jobs and other local development priorities. Constituents consequently hold them politically accountable for development outcomes, although formal responsibility for local development rests principally within the District Assembly system. He noted that the Government’s 2026 Position Paper on constitutional reform has itself acknowledged this institutional evolution, describing MPs as having become development agents in their constituencies “by default” and rejecting a recommendation that DACF allocations to MPs be prohibited. Dr Tando said the development raises a wider accountability question that Ghana must confront before creating another independently elected political office within substantially the same territorial development space. “If both the MP and MMDCE acquire separate democratic legitimacy within substantially the same development space, who ultimately bears political accountability for constituency development when things go right or wrong?” he asked. He said the proposed alternative would shift appointment control away from the Presidency and place responsibility closer to an already elected constituency representative. Under his proposal, however, an MP would not possess unrestricted discretion to appoint any preferred political actor. Dr Tando proposes a regulated system under which relevant public institutions provide professional safeguards around the appointment process. The Public Services Commission could establish appropriate professional and person specifications, while the role and performance expectations of the MMDCE would align with the applicable district development framework and national development planning architecture. He argues that such safeguards could make competence an integral part of the appointment process while retaining identifiable political accountability. The proposal, he acknowledged, represents a significant departure from both the current presidential appointment system and competing proposals for direct popular election. However, he argued that Ghana’s local government debate should not treat an additional election as synonymous with decentralisation. According to him, election addresses the method through which an officeholder acquires political legitimacy, whereas effective decentralisation also requires attention to authority, administrative capacity, resources, planning, coordination and accountability. Dr Tando further questioned whether Ghana should create two separately elected political centres that face substantially overlapping constituency-development expectations without first defining the relationship between their mandates. He maintained that his proposal seeks to institutionalise an existing political reality rather than create an entirely new role for MPs. “We continue to hold MPs politically accountable for local development irrespective of the formal institutional location of development responsibility. Legislation alone is unlikely to erase that deeply embedded political expectation,” he argued. He said the central reform question is therefore whether Ghana should continue to treat that political evolution as an anomaly or deliberately structure, regulate and make it accountable. Dr Tando also called for a broader reconceptualisation of District Assemblies beyond their conventional treatment as local administrative structures. He proposed that the District Assembly should be understood as “a territorial platform through which the fragmented functional state becomes an integrated local service experience in the delivery of public value.” Under that conception, decentralisation should ultimately be assessed through the experience of citizens at the local level rather than principally through the number of functions formally transferred or institutions established. “Decentralisation must make the state coherent at the point where the citizen experiences it,” he said. Dr Tando acknowledged that the MP-led appointment proposal requires further constitutional and institutional scrutiny, including safeguards against excessive concentration of political authority and arrangements for districts that contain more than one parliamentary constituency. He nevertheless argued that unconventional proposals should remain open to scrutiny as Ghana searches for durable consensus on local government reform. “Perhaps MP appointment is not ultimately the answer. I am open to that. But we should not discard the institutional problem simply because one proposed answer is unconventional,” he said.

items.title: Burkina: Une centaine d’enfants initiés aux valeurs du sport et de la discipline par la gendarmerie
items.description: BURKINA-SPORT-SECURITE-CAMP-VACANCES Burkina: Une centaine d’enfants initiés aux valeurs du sport et de la discipline par la gendarmerie Ouagadougou, 14 août 2026 (AIB)- La Gendarmerie nationale a clôturé vendredi, la première édition du camp vacances football, qui a permis d’inculquer à une centaine d’enfants les valeurs de discipline, de respect et d’esprit d’équipe durant un mois, afin de faire d’eux les futurs bâtisseurs du Burkina Faso. « Au-delà de la pratique du football, nous voulions offrir aux enfants un espace d’éducation, de loisirs sains et d’épanouissement, où le sport devient un véritable outil de formation humaine. Notre conviction est qu’investir dans l’enfant aujourd’hui, c’est investir dans l’homme et dans la nation de demain », a déclaré le promoteur, l’adjudant-chef Herman Zabsonré. Il a également expliqué qu’au-delà des performances sportives, il a constaté la naissance de nouvelles amitiés, le développement de l’esprit d’équipe et une meilleure compréhension des valeurs citoyennes. L’adjudant-chef Zabsonré a, par ailleurs, ajouté que les séances de sensibilisation ont permis aux enfants d’acquérir des outils leur permettant de promouvoir la paix autour d’eux. « Au regard des activités réalisées, nous pouvons affirmer avec satisfaction que les objectifs poursuivis ont été atteints. Les enfants ont renforcé leurs connaissances techniques et tactiques en football. Ils ont appris à jouer collectivement, à respecter les règles, à faire preuve de fair-play et à accepter aussi bien la victoire que la défaite avec dignité », a-t-il soutenu. Selon le parrain de la cérémonie, Mahamadou Sawadogo, le football enseigne la discipline, le respect, l’esprit d’équipe et le sens de l’effort. Il s’est dit convaincu que les connaissances acquises sur le terrain contribueront à faire des enfants de futurs citoyens engagés pour leur pays. « Nous avons surtout appris que le véritable champion est celui qui respecte ses adversaires, écoute ses éducateurs, encourage ses coéquipiers et fait preuve de discipline », a déclaré le représentant des participants, Nolan Sawadogo. Il a assuré que les différentes séances de sensibilisation leur ont permis de mieux comprendre l’importance du civisme, du patriotisme, du respect des symboles de leur pays, de la solidarité et du vivre-ensemble. « Ils repartent convaincus que chacun d’eux peut contribuer, à son niveau, à construire un Burkina Faso uni, paisible et prospère », a-t-il confié. Le promoteur a enfin appelé les participants à devenir des ambassadeurs des valeurs qu’ils ont apprises et à faire rayonner autour d’eux le respect, la solidarité, le patriotisme, la paix et la cohésion sociale. items.title: Mali: le Premier ministre reçoit le Secrétaire général adjoint des Nations Unies, Haoliang Xu
items.description: Le Premier ministre, le Général de Division Abdoulaye Maïga a reçu ce vendredi 14 août 2026, au nom de Son Excellence le Général d’Armée Assimi Goïta, Président de la Transition, Chef de l’État, le Secrétaire général adjoint des Nations Unies et Administrateur adjoint du Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD), Haoliang Xu. Dans le cadre de sa tournée sahélienne, il est en visite à Bamako dans le but de renforcer la coopération dans les domaines de l’économie, de l’administration territoriale et de la réconciliation. Pour l’hôte du jour, il s’agit de recueillir les réels défis du pays afin de mieux calibrer les apports, d'impulser la dynamique de développement basée sur les priorités nationales, ainsi que de consolider les acquis. Il s’est réjoui de la bonne articulation des priorités de développement, notamment dans le document de la Vision « MALI KURA ƝƐTAASIRA KA BƐN SAN 2063 MA », ainsi que la Stratégie Nationale pour l'Emergence et le Développement Durable (SNEDD) 2024-2033. En réponse, le Premier ministre a exprimé sa satisfaction pour l’accompagnement dont le Mali bénéficie de la part du PNUD et l’engagement du programme à respecter les principes qui guident l’action publique. Le Premier ministre a rappelé que le Mali entend rester cohérent face à la mise en œuvre efficiente de sa vision qui, a-t-il ajouté, concorde parfaitement avec les objectifs de développement durable du PNUD. Au titre des attentes, il a préconisé une approche onusienne basée sur les particularités et les singularités des États qui font face aux défis sécuritaires, afin d’adapter les interventions aux dimensions environnementale, économique et sociale. Le Chef du gouvernement a également réitéré l’ouverture du Mali à bénéficier davantage de l’accompagnement et de l’expertise du Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement. Source: CCRP-Primature L’article Mali: le Premier ministre reçoit le Secrétaire général adjoint des Nations Unies, Haoliang Xu est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: A Bleak, Violent Novel’s Unexpected Delights
items.description: This is an edition of the Books Briefing, our editors’ weekly guide to the best in books. Sign up for it here. Before his latest book, Marlon James hadn’t written a novel set in Jamaica in more than a decade. In the years following his Booker Prize–winning A Brief History of Seven Killings , the author focused on his Dark Star Trilogy , set in a fantasy universe. But after that long literary detour, he returned to the land of his birth in his new novel, The Disappearers —which is set primarily in Kingston and follows a group of characters, all queer Jamaican men, who meet while rehearsing a play that will never be seen. First, here are four new stories from The Atlantic ’s Books section: Hard-luck men in hardscrabble towns “Disunion,” a short story by Kurt Andersen A deeply layered novel about masculinity “Stance,” a poem by Deborah Garrison For this group, which gathers in secret in 1988, seeing and being seen are matters of life and death. The Kingston they inhabit is murderously homophobic, and accordingly, the novel can be quite bleak. But The Disappearers offers some delights too. Recently, in her article about the book for The Atlantic , Stephanie Burt noted that “the novel opens up many pleasures for literary readers,” who may recognize the numerous titles and references sprinkled throughout. I was deeply affected by how, almost universally, the characters seek out anything that proves that gay life exists on a larger scale. Lowbrow works, such as porn films and magazines, are most accessible; Playgirl and Hustler are name-checked. The songs of Boy George, Sylvester, and Prince are lifelines—the homoerotic cover of Prince’s 1988 album, Lovesexy , is an especially powerful beacon. Many of the characters are well read, and they name-drop gay novels such as Andrew Holleran’s Dancer From the Dance and E. M. Forster’s Maurice . For one of the men in particular, the type of hustling, defiant gay life that John Rechy describes in his nonfiction book The Sexual Outlaw is pivotal. The play they put on, a 1967 drama called Fortune and Men’s Eyes , explores homosexuality among a group of prisoners. Some of its characters see sex as a means for gaining or establishing power; others, as a convenient way to access pleasure. Some are what a modern audience might recognize as gay, whereas others choose partners largely because of their proximity. The cast share the characters’ disparate attitudes toward queerness. But in the Jamaica they live in, there is no room for nuance; any man seen as homosexual is a target for violence. Brutality will soon come to the rehearsal room. In a way, James has written a gay novel about the uses of a gay novel. When his characters invoke Oscar Wilde and Edmund White, Hadrian and Michelangelo, they’re proving, to themselves and to the reader, that queer life existed long before they came around. But James is not an unskeptical cheerleader for the healing power of visibility and representation. The Disappearers ’ major theme, after all, is that being recognized can be a bad thing: Owning these books is a hazard. Buying Lovesexy as a man in 1988 Kingston invites vigilantism. Staging Fortune and Men’s Eyes puts its cast and crew in danger. So why try to do it? The director and ringleader, Havelock Titus, asks himself this question more than a decade after those hopeful rehearsals. He knew, even at the time, that the effort was a risk. He still doesn’t know “what success would have meant,” because the unstaged play “never had the chance to become a failure.” But Havelock knows on some level that he did it because, just like those who came before him, he wanted to create some kind of evidence that gay men communed and survived in his time and place. In short, he was tired of being erased. Illustration by Roche Marlon James Returns to Realism, and to Jamaica By Stephanie Burt In his new novel, gay men struggle to escape violence in Kingston. Read the full article. What to Read The Age of Reform , by Richard Hofstadter History can’t fully explain the present or predict the future, but it can help us understand the patterns of contemporary politics and the likely paths ahead. In 1955, Hofstadter, one of the great American historians of the 20th century, published The Age of Reform —a political and social history of the years 1890 to 1940, the period of populism, progressivism, and the New Deal. Rapid technological change, monopoly power, deep inequality, endemic corruption, mass immigration, nativist demagogues, the transformation of both political parties, repeated efforts at reform, recurring spasms of reaction: Perhaps no other age so resembles our own. Hofstadter is brilliant at analyzing types that feel quite familiar to us today—the crusading urban progressive, the small-town conspiracy theorist. He was a liberal who sympathized with the passion for progress while unsentimentally diagnosing its illiberal ideas and motives. The fevered moralism of that age seems a long way from the paralyzing cynicism of ours. But reading Hofstadter will remind you that reform and reaction not only follow each other, but also often coexist in the same moment; neither ever has the last word. Americans are always dreaming of a better country, and some have actually made it so. — George Packer From our list: What’s the one book that explains American politics today? Out Next Week 📚 Finding Renée Richards , by Julie Kliegman 📚 The Jackal: The Rise and Fall of Carlos, the World’s First Super-Terrorist , by Joby Warrick 📚 The Book of Chuck , by LaToya Watkins Your Weekend Read Illustration by Ben Hickey Bring Back the Blue-Book Exam By Walt Hunter Universities find themselves in a surprising position. The only reliable way to evaluate what students have learned may be to bring back pen and paper. Faculty are reverting to in-person, handwritten assignments and timed essays—anything that keeps assessments offline. The unlikely hero of the day is the blue book, sales of which are up by as much as 80 percent for some universities since 2023. Read the full article. items.title: GSTS honours former Chief of Naval Staff Commodore Stephen Obimpeh at 117th Founders’ Day
items.description: The Ghana Secondary Technical School (GSTS), in collaboration with the GSTS Alumni Association, has honoured former Chief of Naval Staff, Commodore Stephen George Obimpeh (Rtd.), for his distinguished service to Ghana and contributions to leadership, public service, and national development. Commodore Obimpeh, a member of the GSTS Class of 1961, was honoured during the 2026 GSTS Founders’ Day Distinguished Alumni Lecture and Awards, held at the GSTS Auditorium as part of activities marking the school’s 117th anniversary. The celebration was held under the theme, “GSTS @ 117: Developing Resilient Leaders Through Science, Technology and Character.” The event was chaired by Gt. Prof. Anthony Simons, while Gt. Maj. Gen. Matthew K. Essien (Rtd.) delivered the keynote address, which highlighted leadership, resilience, and the importance of preparing young people with the character, knowledge, and technological capabilities required to thrive in an increasingly fast-changing world. Commodore Obimpeh was honoured alongside three other distinguished alumni: Ing. Francis Wouland Tuyee ’54-H4, the first Mayor of Tema Municipality, who was honoured posthumously; Ing. Seth Ahiekpor ’69A-H1; and Prof. Yaw Duodu Yeboah ’69/’71-H2. Speaking on behalf of the 2026 Distinguished Alumni Award recipients, Commodore Obimpeh expressed appreciation to the school and the GSTS Alumni Association for recognising their contributions to society. “On behalf of my fellow 2026 GSTS Distinguished Alumni Award recipients, it is my singular honour and privilege to express our sincere appreciation for the warmth, generosity and dignity with which we have been celebrated today,” he said. He commended the GSTS Alumni Association for sustaining a tradition that recognises service, leadership, and commitment to society, and encouraged current and future generations of Giants to remain committed to service. “May we all be called to service. God bless our homeland Ghana and make our nation great. Giants, Giants, I thank you,” he concluded. A Distinguished Giant and National Servant Commodore Stephen George Obimpeh, born at Vakpo in the Volta Region in 1941, attended the then Government Secondary Technical School, now GSTS, before joining the Ghana Military Academy and later training at the Britannia Royal Naval College in the United Kingdom. He rose through the ranks of the Ghana Navy and became Chief of Naval Staff in 1979. Former Chief of Naval Staff, Commodore Stephen George Obimpeh (Rtd.) After retiring from military service, he continued serving Ghana in several capacities, including coordinating the repatriation of more than 1.2 million Ghanaians from Nigeria during Operation Exodus in 1983. He later served as Member of Parliament for North Dayi, Chairman of Parliament’s Finance Committee, and Minister of Health. He also chaired or served on several national institutions. In recognition of his service to Ghana, Commodore Obimpeh was awarded the national honour of Companion of the Order of the Volta (CV) in 2016. Despite his long career in national service, he has maintained close ties with GSTS and its Alumni Association through mentorship and alumni activities. His recognition at the 2026 Distinguished Alumni Awards therefore celebrated not only his professional achievements and contribution to Ghana, but also his enduring commitment to his alma mater.
